findings.title: Primary lightness flipped from 70% to 30% in light mode
findings.body: The change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The PR's intent (visible throughout the diff) is to keep the light-theme primary lightness the same and only add a complementary secondary for dark themes (e.g. desktop/modal.scss line 94 does 70%/30%). Here the primary value was flipped instead, so `.custom-message-length` text in light mode now renders at 30% lightness instead of the original 70%, producing a much darker color than before.

findings.title: Primary lightness flipped from 30% to 70% in light mode
findings.body: Inside `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a`, the change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Following the convention used elsewhere in the PR (primary lightness preserved, secondary set to the complement, e.g. the next `.arrow` rule on line 294 does 60%/40%), this should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. In light mode the link color is now much lighter than before.

findings.title: Group member name color: primary value altered from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Inside `.group-member-info .name`, the change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. Every other transformation in this PR keeps the primary lightness identical to the original and uses the complement only for `$secondary` (e.g. `.title` immediately below correctly stays at 50%/50% on line 527 because its original was already 50%). Here the primary went from 30% to 50%, so group-member names on user pages render with a noticeably lighter color in light mode.

findings.title: Topic-map h3 color: primary value altered from 20% to 50%
findings.body: Inside `.topic-map h3`, the change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The PR's pattern (see the sibling `.topic-map h4` rule on line 190, which correctly keeps its 50% original) is to leave the primary lightness unchanged and pick the complement for `$secondary`. This one was copied from the h4 rule, so in light mode the topic-map h3 headings now appear far lighter (50%) than they were (20%).

findings.title: Group member name color (mobile): primary value altered from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Inside `.group-member-info .name`, the change replaces `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This is the mobile counterpart of the same pattern bug in desktop/user.scss line 522; it appears the rule was copy-pasted from the sibling `.title` selector (whose original lightness really was 50%). Group-member names on mobile user pages now render at 50% lightness in light mode instead of the original 30%, making them visibly lighter.
